r0.why: Coarse-grained intrusive rock and its four minerals [1]; slow-cooling silica- and alkali-rich magma underground [2]; Latin granum etymology [10].

r1.why: Common in continental crust in intrusions [3]; dikes of centimeters to batholiths over hundreds of km2 [4]; most abundant basement rock, Precambrian [40][41]; batholiths and orogenic ranges [44].

r2.why: Colours by mineralogy [11]; interlocking feldspar-quartz matrix peppered with biotite and amphibole [12]; phenocrysts and porphyritic texture [13]; granite porphyry [14]; massive and tough [8].

r3.why: Granitoid family of coarse quartz and feldspars [5]; classified by relative quartz/alkali feldspar/plagioclase [6]; 20-60% quartz and 35-90% alkali feldspar [21]; syenites, monzonites, granodiorites, tonalites [22].

r4.why: Density 2.65-2.75 and strength above 200 MPa [35]; dry melting 1215-1260 C, down to 650 C with water at a few hundred MPa [36].

r5.why: Tors, domes, bornhardts, massifs [42]; tough and massive properties made it a construction stone [8][9]; microgranite [38]; rhyolite [39].
